title: Victoria Sponge
subtitle: Classic British jam and cream sandwich cake
excerpt: Two light, golden sponge cakes sandwiched with strawberry jam and whipped cream, dusted with icing sugar. The quintessential British celebration cake.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Victoria sponge is named after Queen Victoria, who was known to enjoy a slice of sponge cake with her afternoon tea. It is the defining British cake and the standard by which home bakers are often judged. The recipe follows a simple equal-weight formula: equal quantities in grams of butter, caster sugar, flour, and eggs, which means it can be scaled to any size by simply weighing the eggs and using the same weight of everything else. A proper Victoria sponge uses whipped cream and jam as its filling, not buttercream. The Women's Institute competition rules specify that the jam must be strawberry. The sponges should be flat-topped, well risen, and sprung when pressed.

recipeTools.notes: Two 20 cm round sandwich cake tins, greased and lined.

content.text: Weigh the eggs in their shells: use this weight for the butter, sugar, and flour. Room-temperature butter is essential for a proper cream: cold butter will not beat to a pale, fluffy mixture, and the cake will be dense. Beat the butter and sugar for a full 5 minutes until very pale. The air incorporated during creaming is what makes the sponge light. Divide the batter evenly between the tins by weight.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins. Beat the butter and caster sugar for 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Fold in the flour, vanilla, and milk until just combined.

Divide the batter evenly between the tins and smooth the tops. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the sponges are golden, well risen, and spring back when pressed. Leave in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out and cool completely on a wire rack.
Spread the flat side of one sponge with jam. Spread the whipped cream over the jam. Place the second sponge on top, flat-side down. Dust generously with icing sugar and serve.
